chapter: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
title: Cab Calloway as bandleader: entertainer and disciplinarian

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Cab, well, Cab mostly was an entertainer. And he studied music. I think he studied saxophone with Walter, Foots and some of them, but I guess a man the caliber that Cab was, I mean, couldn't devote too much time to studying music at that part of the game, you know, he was a big top man now you know, what's he going to study saxophone for. He studied it enough you know, and that stage of the game you know I guess he would have been able to be, if he continued, a good saxophone player.
In the way that Billy Eckstein was a decent trumpet player, trombone player.
Yeah, you see that stage of the game they've already made it, they're stars already. Now you've got to

set them down and let them start taking the instruments, starting back there with the ABCs, you know that ain't going to make it too much, you know, and Cab was good. I learned a lot. Cab was very disciplined, his band was.
I remember, Panama Francis took your place, right, eventually?
J. C. Heard took my place, then Panama took J.C.'s.
Because I've looked over Panama's oral history interview and he said that I guess as you said, Cab was very disciplined and he insisted on the band being punctual and sober ...

Like, you know, how they used to have cliques in bands, Cab says I'll fire the clique. You know, he never stood for any foolishness, which was good, very good discipline, nobody, everybody was there on time. You know paying that kind of money you know, and he was very good, he wouldn't repimand anybody unless they caused him to do so. He was very strict.

I think Panama mentioned that there was, or maybe it was Milt Hinton mentioned that there was a ritual about if you got a certain color check that meant that you were still on the band, but if you got like a pink check, that meant that you got your two weeks' notice, something like that.
Well I didn't experience that while I was in the band, maybe that happened later when Panama was in there. But Cab, oh he was just great, great to work for.
